I’ve been feeling this heavy cloud over me for more than a year now—like I’m underwater, watching life move from far away. As an art student, I used to lose myself in painting, but now I can’t even open my sketchbook. I just sit there, staring. My thoughts feel slow and muddled, like I’m pushing through fog just to remember what I was thinking a second ago. The sadness doesn’t lift. Some days, I plan how I’d do it—specific, like taking pills when my roommate’s away for the weekend. I’ve even written something out, just in case.

But there’s more. Lately, I’ve been hearing whispers when no one’s around—like someone murmuring my name from another room. And sometimes… I get these flashes of certainty that I’m meant for something huge. Like I’m not just an art student—I’m a visionary, chosen to reveal some hidden truth through my work. It sounds crazy, I know, but it feels so real when I hear it in my head. I can’t tell if it’s hope or something breaking. The voices come and go, and so does that sense of purpose—some days I’m nobody, others I’m destined for fame. I don’t know what’s real anymore.
D015-D007_h001.question_a:
I’ve been feeling completely empty for over a year now—like I’m moving through fog. I can’t even pick up a paintbrush anymore, which kills me because art was everything. My thoughts feel slow and cloudy, like I’m always dazed, and I can’t concentrate long enough to sketch, let alone finish a piece. I’ve stopped going to class, stopped seeing friends. I just stay in bed. 

Lately, I’ve been hearing voices—usually a man’s voice telling me I’m a failed artist, that I’ll never matter. Sometimes it says the opposite—that I’m actually a chosen visionary, destined to reveal profound truths through paintings no one’s seen yet. I know it doesn’t make sense, but in the moment, it feels real. These voices only come when I’m deep in this depressive spiral. When I’m not feeling this low, they disappear. 

I’ve thought about ending it—planned it out, actually. There’s a bridge near campus I pass every day. I keep imagining jumping at night when no one’s around. I’ve even timed when the streetlights flicker so I wouldn’t be seen. I don’t want to die, but I don’t know how to keep living like this.
D015-D007_h001.question_b:
I’ve been feeling really down for over a year now—like, constantly heavy, like I’m moving through fog. Things I used to love, like painting or even going to class, just feel pointless. I can’t focus—the thoughts are just… blurry, like my brain’s wrapped in cotton. Some days, I lie in bed making exact plans: where I’d go, how I’d do it, what it would look like. I’ve picked out a time and place more than once.

But it’s not just the depression. For as long as I can remember, I’ve heard voices—sometimes whispering my name, other times telling me I’m destined to be a visionary, that my art will change the world in ways no one understands yet. I *know* I’m not famous now, but there are moments—clear moments—when I’m not depressed at all, and the voices are still there, and that feeling of greatness stays. I’ve had stretches—more than a few weeks—where I wasn’t crying every day or feeling completely worthless, but the voices didn’t stop. They just kept talking, kept telling me I’m special. That’s when I know this is more than just depression.

D015-D007_h025.question_both:
I’ve been crying a lot lately—like, out of nowhere. I’ll be reviewing a contract or just sitting in traffic, and suddenly I’m sobbing. It’s been going on for… I don’t know, around eight months now? Definitely affecting my work. I used to thrive on billable hours, but now I can’t focus. I sleep constantly—like, I’ll come home and crash for 12 hours, then nap after dinner. But I’m still exhausted. I barely eat anymore; food just feels like a chore.  

And the guilt… God, I feel like I’m failing everyone. My husband, my clients, even strangers on the subway—I’ll think, *I should’ve held the door longer,* and spiral into this idea that I’ve ruined someone’s day. I know it sounds irrational, but it feels true.  

There are times, especially at night, when I feel someone touching me—like fingers brushing my arm or the sheets shifting when no one’s there. And sometimes… I get this certainty that my old professor, someone I haven’t seen in years, still watches me, cares for me deeply. We’ve never been involved, but in my mind, I *know* he’s waiting for me.  

I can’t tell if these thoughts come from the sadness or if they’re separate. The lines feel blurred.
D015-D007_h025.question_a:
I’ve been struggling almost every day for about eight months now. As a corporate lawyer, my job used to be my strength, but lately I can’t concentrate, I cry during meetings, and I’ve had to call in sick multiple times because I sleep 10 or 11 hours and still feel exhausted. I wake up feeling like I’ve failed my family—even for small things, like not answering my husband’s text quickly enough. I don’t eat much anymore; food just makes me nauseous. 

About three months ago, things got worse. I became convinced my senior partner, a man I’ve barely spoken to, was secretly in love with me—sending me signals in emails, lingering in the hallway just to be near me. I know it sounds irrational, but it felt real. I’d feel fingers brushing my arm when no one was there, especially at night. But here’s the thing: whenever I’ve felt even slightly better—like during a weekend getaway last month—those thoughts and sensations disappeared completely. They only come back when I’m deep in this dark cloud of sadness. I’m only psychotic when I’m in the worst of the depression.
D015-D007_h025.question_b:
I’ve been crying all the time—sometimes for no reason at all. It’s been going on for about eight months now. As a corporate lawyer, I used to thrive under pressure, but lately, I can’t get myself to work on time because I sleep too much. I’ll go to bed at 8 p.m. and wake up at 2 a.m., then nap during the day. Food doesn’t interest me anymore—I’ve lost a lot of weight. I keep thinking I’ve failed my family, my clients, my husband… like I’ve ruined everything and deserve to be punished.  

But even when I was having those thoughts, there were times—times when I wasn’t feeling depressed—when I still knew deep down that Sarah, my junior partner, was secretly in love with me. She gives me no signs, but I *know* it’s true. And sometimes, even now, I feel fingers brushing my arm or someone touching my neck when no one’s there.  

The thing is, a few weeks ago, I had a stretch where I wasn’t sad at all—felt almost normal—but those feelings on my skin and the certainty about Sarah were still there. That’s when I realized this isn’t just depression. It’s something else sticking around, even when the sadness lifts.
